findings.title: Unknown Threat Actor Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Target South Korean Finance
findings.summary_md: CrowdStrike Intelligence identified late September to early October 2026 activity against South Korean financial organizations that used ARTEX alongside large language models. The actor-controlled open directories exposed Claude Code session histories, ARTEX configuration files and Claude memory files, showing a two-server setup with DeepSeek v4.1-flash as the ARTEX backend plus GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 in Claude Code sessions. CrowdStrike assessed the actor as likely Chinese-speaking and financially motivated with moderate confidence and did not attribute the campaign to a named adversary.

findings.title: ARTEX AI, Claude agents used in cyberattacks on South Korean banks
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported on 10 October 2026 that a Chinese-speaking attacker used ARTEX and Claude agents against South Korean financial organizations earlier that month, based on CrowdStrike's confirmation and infrastructure review. Researchers found open directories with Claude Code session histories, ARTEX configuration files and Claude memory files, and identified DeepSeek v4.1-flash as the primary model with GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 also in use. The report said the developer moved ARTEX to closed source and discontinued updates after confirming malicious use.

findings.title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
findings.summary_md: Microsoft tied Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor active since 2021, to ARTEX-driven attacks against hundreds of organizations and the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain compromise. Between 10 and 14 October 2026 the actor ran a cross-tenant password spray against 327 accounts at eight organizations from 144.172.64[.]99, generating more than 151,000 failed logons and peaking at 2,900 failures per minute. Microsoft said privileged access followed in under three hours in several cases and advised reviewing service principal sign-ins and preserving evidence while following ConnectWise containment guidance.

findings.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
findings.summary_md: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported that threat actors were using the ARTEX agentic framework to search public GitHub repositories for exposed secrets, including OAuth application credentials and AI service API keys, then use them against cloud tenants. Starting in August 2026 the agents sent high volumes of targeted GitHub queries; in one observed case an agent moved from finding a client secret to exfiltrating data from Azure Key Vault in five minutes. Microsoft also saw service principal sign-ins from 199.19.77[.]84 as early as 28 October 2026, and advised revoking or rotating exposed credentials rather than only deleting the source code.

findings.title: ARTEX: Agentic Asbestos
findings.summary_md: Censys counted 1,465 hosts serving an exposed ARTEX console as of 4 November 2026, about 650 of them in two identically configured hosting blocks, leaving roughly 815 distinct-looking deployments. It found 155 ARTEX hosts also running another Censys-detected threat, 32 open directories on ARTEX hosts, and a default console port of 8787/tcp. Censys scan history showed an open directory on the host named in the South Korean finance case from 18 August 2026, seven weeks before that report was published.

findings.title: Hacking on Autopilot: Inside ARTEX Cybercrime Campaigns
findings.summary_md: Check Point Research analyzed operator-side artifacts from ARTEX deployments and found 2,557 systems hosting or having hosted ARTEX panels, with 1,608 live public instances at the time of research; ten instances exposed the full ARTEX database. The exposed databases showed operators mostly using Chinese LLM families, led by DeepSeek Flash, for campaigns aimed at cryptocurrency theft, code-signing certificate theft, gaming credentials and denial of service. Check Point noted guardrails appearing only with Anthropic's Opus 5.5, after which an operator switched to more permissive models.

findings.title: ARTEX: AI Agents Find and Abuse Exposed GitHub Secrets
findings.summary_md: GitGuardian summarized Microsoft's ARTEX reporting and argued the exposed-secret problem predates the tool: its State of Secrets Sprawl 2026 counted 28.65 million new hardcoded secrets in 2025 and found 64% of valid secrets leaked in 2022 still active in 2026. The post described two unauthenticated checks, GET /api/health and GET /api/auth/status, that identify an ARTEX console and whether first-run setup is complete. It cited roughly 1,400 exposed instances from Censys as of 4 November and more than 1,800 from Check Point on 5 November, noting the two counts use different methods.

findings.title: Beyond ARTEX: 45 AI Pentesting Tools and How to Find Them
findings.summary_md: GitGuardian cataloged about 45 open-source agentic penetration-testing frameworks around ARTEX, sorting 32 of them into five families. Only four shipped a secret scanner wired to the agent, and none included a GitHub fetcher, leaving the model to assemble the rest at runtime. The post matched the ARTEX family to 1,428 Shodan services on 7 November 2026, and noted 102 forks and ARTEX-named repositories appeared in the week of the 8 October takedown.

findings.title: ARTEX finds leaked secrets without a scanner: lab test
findings.summary_md: GitGuardian ran an ARTEX build in a sealed lab against a fake GitHub repository with nine planted credentials and found eight of them without any secret-scanning tool. The model improvised the hunt with git log --all, git show and grep, starting 6 to 13 seconds into the task, and did the same under a neutral prompt that never mentioned secrets. Only two of the nine canaries were in files at HEAD; the model recovered an AWS key deleted one commit after it was added, and it made no attempts to use any credential it found.

findings.title: Threat Overview of ARTEX Autonomous Penetration Testing Framework
findings.summary_md: FBI FLASH-20261113-001 says malicious actors had used ARTEX since at least August 2026 against organizations in sectors including financial services, government, technology, defense, semiconductors, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, telecommunications and legal services. It states that some intrusions moved from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours, and cites roughly 67,000 individuals affected in South Korean financial attacks and attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 downstream ConnectWise tenants. The FLASH reports over 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX consoles in early November, says the framework persists through forks and ARTEX PRO after the October GitHub removal, and notes that endpoint protection blocked lateral movement to domain controllers in observed activity.
